concepts.label: Computer Systems and Levels of Abstraction

study_sequence.directive: Explain how computer systems are organized as interacting components (hardware and software) and how abstraction layers let us reason about complex systems by hiding lower-level details.

Explain that computation operates over representations of information (data), and summarize why choosing an appropriate representation affects what operations are possible and how efficiently they run.
Define computation as a process of transforming inputs to outputs and explain what it means to frame a real-world goal as a well-specified problem that can be computed.
Describe an algorithm as a finite, unambiguous sequence of steps for solving a problem, and distinguish the problem statement from a particular algorithm that solves it.
Introduce why resource usage (time/space) matters, give an informal account of how input size affects running time, and connect efficiency concerns to algorithm and data-structure choices.
State how programs encode algorithms in a programming language for execution by a computer system, and clarify the relationship among algorithm, program, and machine execution.
